transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-27
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Aaron Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), John Mercer (Lakeshore CTO), Maria Ruiz (Lakeshore Head of Security), Liam O'Neill (SRE), Kavita Sharma (Product)

Summary: Quick product walkthrough focused on data handling and retention controls in Redwood Console and Redwood Optimize. Demo covered request storage toggles, logging redaction, PII detection, audit logs, KMS/HSM options, and Dedicated/private deployment considerations. Customer concerned about PCI card data, EU residency, and SOC2 compliance. Next steps agreed: send security pack, schedule technical deep dive, run a pilot with request-level storage off for sensitive routes.

Transcript:
[00:00] Aaron: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Aaron Chen from Redwood, I'll run through the data retention and logging controls, and Priya will jump into the console demo.
[00:12] John: Thanks Aaron. High-level we need to validate Redwood can meet our PCI and data residency requirements before we move forward. Maria from security will lead that side.
[00:20] Maria: Yep, key things for us: ability to disable request storage at route level, PII redaction in logs, KMS/HSM for key management, and auditable retention policy that we can show to auditors.
[00:30] Aaron: Totally, that's what we're demoing today. Quick agenda: show Console toggles, how Optimize recommends retention/quantization, and then how Dedicated/private differs for on-prem or VPC.
[00:42] Priya: Quick note, transcription or auto captions might spell some of our product bits odd — you might see "Reedwood" or "K V cash" — apologies in advance.
[00:50] Liam: ha, been there. ok go ahead.
[01:05] Priya: Alright sharing screen, starting in the Redwood Console. First panel is Project settings -> Data handling. Here you can toggle request storage at the route level. For example we have a payments-route where we set Request Storage: OFF. That means full request bodies are not persisted to our long-term blob store or logs.
[01:30] John: When you say "not persisted" is anything still captured for debugging? ephemeral traces or just headers?
[01:38] Priya: Good question. We keep a short-lived trace buffer for in-flight debugging (default 15 minutes) and scrubbed telemetry for metrics. If Request Storage is OFF we do not write the raw request to object storage. You can also enable "redact on ingest" which runs a PII detection filter and replaces tokens with [REDACTED].
[01:58] Maria: Is the PII detector configurable? we need to catch card numbers, full PANs, CVV, and also custom ids.
[02:08] Priya: Yes, the redaction module ships with pre-built detectors for PAN, SSN, emails, etc. There is a rules engine to add custom regex or enterprise classifiers. We also support hashed tokens — so instead of storing full fields, we store a one-way hash if you want to correlate without retaining raw values.
[02:24] John: Is hashing done client-side or server-side? we prefer customer-managed keys if possible.
[02:30] Priya: You can choose. By default we perform server-side hashing using a Redwood-managed key, but for Dedicated or Private deployments you can bring-your-own-key via KMS or HSM integrations. That option is in the key management tab.
[02:42] Maria: For auditors, can we get exportable proof of where data was stored and when it was deleted?
[02:49] Aaron: Yes, audit logs include retention actions, deletion events, and S3 lifecycle actions. We surface those in the console and you can stream them to your SIEM (Splunk/Datadog) or pull via API. Note: exports are also subject to retention settings.
[03:05] [03:05] Priya: jumping to the Audit Logs page — you can filter by event type: DATA_RETENTION_POLICY_UPDATED, REQUEST_STORAGE_TOGGLE, REDACTION_RULE_CHANGED. Example entry: 2026-03-15T12:11:22Z — REQUEST_STORAGE_TOGGLE — user: admin@lakeshore.co — route: payments-route — previous: ON -> OFF.
[03:30] Liam: What about network isolation? we can't send raw payloads to a multi-tenant blob store.
[03:36] Priya: For Dedicated we provision isolated GPU pools and customer-specific object storage buckets; for Private you can host the object store in your VPC or on-prem S3-compatible store.
[03:46] Maria: And data residency? We're EU-based for payments, need EU-only storage.
[03:52] Aaron: You can pin storage regions; for Hosted we support EU regions and we can pin buckets to eu-west-1, etc. For strict residency you can use Dedicated or Private to guarantee no egress.
[04:05] John: Ok good. Now show the console flow for setting a retention window.
[04:12] Priya: Sure — navigating to Retention Policies. We can set retention by project, by dataset, or by route. Example: payments-route retention 30 days, logs retention 7 days, metrics 365 days. There's also a "legal hold" toggle that prevents deletion for a given asset id.
[04:28] Maria: If I enable legal hold, does that override request-level OFF? we need to ensure legal holds don't inadvertently retain raw payloads if storage is turned off.
[04:36] Priya: Legal hold only applies to items already stored. If Request Storage was OFF at time of request, there's no raw payload to hold. Legal hold prevents lifecycle deletions of objects that exist. We also show provenance metadata for each object.
[04:50] John: How do you handle third-party logs — like streaming logs or traces that might contain PII?
[04:56] Aaron: We recommend enabling redact-on-ingest for any log ingestion pipeline. For streaming we provide a pre-ingest webhook that runs PII filters before the object is persisted. Cognitively there might be occasional false positives or negatives, we surface scoring so you can review redaction decisions and tune rules.
[05:18] [05:18] Priya: moving to Redwood Optimize — this is our suggestions engine. It will recommend batching, cache settings, and quantization that also impact what we store. For example, Optimize can suggest enabling prefix caching for non-sensitive routes and turning off KV cache persistence for sensitive routes.
[05:36] Kavita: I'm curious about the KV cache persistence mention, what exactly persists? session keys or partial context?
[05:43] Priya: The KV cache stores key-value state for attention cache and can be persisted for faster warm starts. You can mark cache persistence as OFF for routes handling PII — then KV is regenerated on warm-up but not written to disk. We call out this setting in the model config.
[06:00] Liam: Performance hit then, right? what's the latency delta?
[06:05] Priya: Usually 5-20% higher cold-start latency depending on sequence length. That's why Optimize suggests tradeoffs by profiling your workload.
[06:14] John: Can we do a demo of toggling storage on a live route?
[06:20] Priya: Sure, I'll use a sandbox project. Going to payments-route — flipping Request Storage: OFF -> SAVE. Note the audit log entry: REQUEST_STORAGE_TOGGLE generated immediately. Backend does a policy check and will apply the setting for new incoming requests; existing stored objects are unaffected.
[06:37] Maria: I see the audit line but the transcript shows "req storage toggled off" — sometimes your UI shows slight delay correct?
[06:44] Priya: There can be a couple-second propagation delay across control plane regions; we show a banner when change is pushed.
[06:50] [06:50] Aaron: Quick aside: many customers ask whether Redwood inspects data for model feedback loops — e.g., do we use customer inputs to improve models? By default we do not use customer data to train public models; we have an opt-in for telemetry-based improvements and an explicit "no-train" toggle at project level.
[07:10] Maria: We need explicit no-train for payments. Also want assurance that derivative artifacts (embeddings, logs) aren't used.
[07:18] Aaron: Absolutely — you can set Project -> Data Use: "No Training, No Derivative Storage". That prevents embeddings from being stored and blocks downstream model feedback loops.
[07:26] John: About function calling and tool outputs — sometimes tools will return sensitive PII (like full PAN) in the model response. How do you redaction responses?
[07:34] Priya: There's an output redaction pipeline that can apply rules to model responses before they hit customers or logs. You can choose to redact in-flight or post-process. If you choose to redact in-flight we can strip or mask fields before sending back to your app.
[07:50] Liam: Will that affect latency?
[07:53] Priya: Minimal, usually a few ms per request depending on rules complexity.
[07:58] John: Ok, show KMS integration flow.
[08:02] Priya: Key Management tab: we support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, and HSM via PKCS#11. For BYOK you upload the public key and configure envelope encryption; Redwood never stores your key material. We also provide key rotation events in audit logs.
[08:20] Maria: For HSM rotations, can those be automated with our HSM provider?
[08:25] Priya: Yes, we support rotation hooks and can integrate with your HSM provider to trigger rotation and push rotation metadata to the audit log.
[08:33] [08:33] Aaron: Another common ask: can we run a point-in-time delete for a given customer id across all storage? We have a Data Subject Rights API that accepts an identifier and will orchestrate deletion across object stores, indices, and embeddings. The operation is auditable and returns a job id.
[08:52] Maria: Does that also scrub backups? we have backups retained off-site for 90 days.
[08:58] Priya: We have a backup retention policy — the delete job will mark items for deletion and initiate lifecycle deletions; for immutable backups we can provide a certified deletion process or place items in a legal review queue. This is a nuance—if your backups are immutable snapshots in a separate system we need to coordinate deletion with that system and we provide the audit trail for that coordination.
[09:20] John: Ok good to know. Let's talk SLAs for Dedicated.
[09:24] Aaron: Dedicated includes capacity guarantees and region pinning; we offer SLA-backed latency targets and a dedicated object store. There's also an option for private control plane.
[09:33] Liam: If we pick Dedicated in eu-west-1, can we control egress between zones?
[09:38] Priya: Yes, you can restrict egress and pin to single AZ if you want, though that limits HA. We usually recommend multi-AZ with private peering to your VPC.
[09:50] [09:50] Maria: Any real-world gotchas? things customers forget to do when configuring redaction?
[09:55] Priya: Two common ones — 1) forgetting to enable redact-on-ingest on third-party log streams; 2) enabling legal hold inadvertently without realizing it prevents lifecycle deletion. We added UI warnings for both.
[10:08] John: Can we demo the Data Subject Rights API?
[10:12] Priya: Quick demo — hitting POST /dsr/delete with { "customer_id": "acct-1234" } — returns job id jd-20260327-01. Then you can GET status and see what objects were affected. Note: we will only delete objects that exist and match the identifier; if some items are in immutable cold storage, the job will list them and route to legal review.
[10:35] Liam: about logs — we plan to forward app logs to your ingest pipeline; do you provide pre-ingest transforms?
[10:41] Priya: Yes, you can attach a transform lambda that runs before persistence. We provide a managed lambda framework with templates for redaction.
[10:49] [10:49] Aaron: We try to make it easy to map security requirements to settings: route-level toggles, project-level defaults, and account-level controls.
[11:00] Maria: How does the console surface redaction hits? we need a report for auditors showing number of redactions and examples (sanitized).
[11:06] Priya: We have Redaction Insights: dashboards that show counts, types, top patterns, and a sample view with masked context. You can export the report as CSV/PDF for auditors.
[11:18] John: Great. Anything on retention defaults — what are they for hosted?
[11:22] Aaron: Hosted defaults are 30 days for requests, 90 days for logs, 365 days for metrics. But customers often change that; default policies are documented in the security pack we'll share.
[11:33] [11:33] Priya: moving into an example flow: we'll send a synthetic request with PAN-like content to the sandbox, show it being redacted and then show it's not present in object storage when Request Storage is OFF.
[11:45] Priya: Sending request now... request payload: { "name": "Jane Doe", "card": "4111 1111 1111 1111", "amount": 39.99 }.
[11:56] [11:56] Priya: In logs we see the redaction score 0.98 and the response shows "card": "[REDACTED]". Also payload is not written to bucket because Request Storage was OFF at the route level.
[12:10] Maria: The sample looks good, any chance of false negative on unusual PAN formats?
[12:16] Priya: It's possible; that's why we allow rule overrides and manual review queues. We surface an alert when a high-confidence potential PII pattern is unredacted.
[12:26] John: Ok we're comfortable so far. Let's talk about production rollout — pilot scope and success criteria.
[12:33] Aaron: Most pilots are 2-4 weeks, include a set of sensitive routes with Request Storage OFF, run sample traffic to measure latency and error rates, and then evaluate redaction performance (precision/recall) on a held-out dataset.
[12:48] Kavita: Success criteria: no raw PAN stored, <1% redaction false negatives on test set, latency within 10% of baseline.
[12:56] Aaron: Sounds reasonable. We'll provide a checklist in the pilot docs.
[13:02] [13:02] Priya: Quick note on billing: when Request Storage is OFF you'll still be charged for compute and tokens; storage charges are lower because objects aren't written. Optimize can estimate cost savings from toggling storage.
[13:16] John: Good. On legal/contract side — we need contract language for data handling.
[13:21] Aaron: We'll send a security appendix with contract clauses for data residency, no-train, and deletion obligations. Legal can review.
[13:30] Maria: One more: if there is a data breach, what's your incident response and notification timeline?
[13:35] Aaron: We have an incident response plan with 72-hour notification for confirmed breaches, and we work through joint response playbooks. For Dedicated customers we provide faster escalation.
[13:47] [13:47] Priya: going to show the private deployment diagram real quick— control plane in your VPC, optional on-prem object store, and egress rules.
[13:58] Priya: (diagram shows SAML SSO integration, audit log streaming, and monitoring hooks).
[14:06] Liam: what's the SSO provisioning flow? SCIM?
[14:10] Priya: SCIM provisioning and SAML for login, with RBAC of course. You can map groups to roles like Admin, Developer, Ops.
[14:20] John: Any limitations on exports for compliance? e.g., can we get a full export of all audit logs for last 2 years?
[14:27] Aaron: For Hosted we retain logs per your retention policies; longer term retention can be exported to your bucket. For Dedicated/Private we can set retention to match your requests and export a complete dataset on demand.
[14:40] [14:40] Maria: ok let's confirm next steps quickly.
[14:44] Aaron: Recap: we'll send SOC2 + security pack and sample retention configs; Priya will schedule a deep technical session to validate network topology and BYOK; John will provide sample payloads and success criteria; and we'll provision a pilot sandbox that flips request storage and runs test traffic.
[15:02] John: Sounds good. Any final quick Qs?
[15:06] Kavita: one more on embeddings — we plan to use embeddings for search, will those be considered derivative data?
[15:12] Priya: Embeddings are derivative artifacts; you can opt-out of storing embeddings or store them in your own bucket. If you choose no-derivatives, they won't be persisted.
[15:24] Maria: ok thanks. That covers our main concerns.
[15:28] Aaron: Great. We'll follow up with the docs and schedule. Thanks everyone.

End of transcript.

Notes on transcription quality: moderate; occasional mis-hearings and product names slightly garbled in automated captions.
